encrypted_dns_enabled.title: Encrypted DNS Enabled
encrypted_dns_enabled.description: Whether DNS queries are transmitted using an encryption protocol such as DNS-over-TLS (DoT), DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH), or DNS-over-QUIC (DoQ) instead of plaintext UDP/TCP port 53.

dns_transport_protocol.title: DNS Transport Protocol
dns_transport_protocol.description: The protocol used to transmit DNS queries between clients and resolvers.

dnssec_validation_enabled.title: DNSSEC Validation Enabled
dnssec_validation_enabled.description: Whether the DNS resolver is configured to perform DNSSEC cryptographic signature validation on responses, providing integrity protection that defeats cache poisoning and response spoofing even when transaction ID or source port entropy is low.

dnssec_signing_configured.title: DNSSEC Zone Signing Configured
dnssec_signing_configured.description: Whether authoritative DNS zones served by this system are signed with DNSSEC keys (DNSKEY/RRSIG records present).

dot_enforcement_mode.title: DNS-over-TLS Enforcement Mode
dot_enforcement_mode.description: Whether DoT (port 853) is mandatory, optional, or disabled for DNS clients. 'enforced' means plaintext DNS is blocked and only DoT is allowed. 'opportunistic' means DoT is attempted but plaintext fallback is permitted. 'disabled' means only plaintext DNS is used.

plaintext_dns_port_53_blocked.title: Plaintext DNS Port 53 Egress Blocked
plaintext_dns_port_53_blocked.description: Whether outbound UDP/TCP port 53 traffic from DNS clients is blocked at the network layer (firewall/security group), preventing fallback to cleartext DNS even if a client attempts it.

dot_upstream_resolver_configured.title: DoT-capable Upstream Resolver Configured
dot_upstream_resolver_configured.description: Whether a DNS-over-TLS capable upstream resolver (e.g., 1.1.1.1:853, 8.8.8.8:853, or internal DoT resolver) is explicitly configured for use on port 853.

source_port_randomization_enabled.title: Source Port Randomization Enabled
source_port_randomization_enabled.description: Whether the DNS resolver uses randomized ephemeral source ports for outgoing queries as specified in RFC 5452. Disabled or restricted port ranges dramatically reduce entropy and enable birthday-attack cache poisoning.

transaction_id_entropy_bits.title: DNS Transaction ID Entropy (bits)
transaction_id_entropy_bits.description: The effective entropy in bits used for DNS transaction ID generation. The standard 16-bit TXID field provides at most 65535 values; weak or predictable PRNG reduces this. Values below 16 indicate predictable IDs susceptible to birthday attacks.

zone_transfer_enabled.title: Zone Transfer Enabled
zone_transfer_enabled.description: Whether the DNS server is configured to serve AXFR or IXFR zone transfer requests to secondaries or other clients.

zone_transfer_tls_enabled.title: Zone Transfer TLS Enabled
zone_transfer_tls_enabled.description: Whether AXFR/IXFR zone transfer sessions are wrapped in TLS (DNS-over-TLS or equivalent channel encryption).

transfer_acl_restricted.title: Zone Transfer ACL Restricted
transfer_acl_restricted.description: Whether zone transfers are restricted to a defined set of authorized secondary server IP addresses via an access control list.

tsig_authentication_enabled.title: TSIG Authentication Enabled
tsig_authentication_enabled.description: Whether Transaction Signature (TSIG) or SIG(0) keys are required to authenticate DNS messages (zone transfers and/or client-to-resolver), providing cryptographic authentication and integrity even if the channel is not encrypted.

resolver_certificate_validation_enforced.title: Resolver Certificate Validation Enforced
resolver_certificate_validation_enforced.description: Whether the DNS client enforces validation of the resolver's TLS certificate (checking CA chain, hostname, and expiry) when DoT or DoH is in use, preventing impersonation by rogue resolvers.

tsig_algorithm.title: TSIG HMAC Algorithm
tsig_algorithm.description: The HMAC algorithm negotiated for TSIG transaction signatures on DNS messages.

tsig_clock_skew_seconds.title: TSIG Allowed Clock Skew (Seconds)
tsig_clock_skew_seconds.description: The maximum permitted time difference in seconds between the signing time in a TSIG record and the server's current time, defining the replay protection window.

tsig_key_configured.title: TSIG Key Configured
tsig_key_configured.description: Indicates whether at least one TSIG shared secret key is configured on the DNS server for transaction authentication.

dns_response_rate_limiting_enabled.title: DNS Response Rate Limiting Enabled
dns_response_rate_limiting_enabled.description: Whether DNS Response Rate Limiting (RRL) is configured on the DNS server/resolver to throttle repeated responses to the same query pattern, mitigating amplification and flood attacks.

recursive_queries_publicly_accessible.title: Recursive DNS Queries Publicly Accessible
recursive_queries_publicly_accessible.description: Whether the DNS server accepts and processes recursive queries from arbitrary source IPs on the public internet, enabling open resolver abuse for amplification attacks.

dnssec_enabled.title: DNSSEC Enabled on Authoritative Server
dnssec_enabled.description: Whether DNSSEC is enabled on the DNS server, which significantly increases response sizes for signed zones and can substantially raise the amplification ratio when combined with open recursion.

doh_enabled.title: DNS-over-HTTPS Enabled
doh_enabled.description: Whether DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) is configured and in use by clients or resolvers in the environment.

certificate_pinning_enforced.title: Certificate Pinning Enforced for DoH
certificate_pinning_enforced.description: Whether certificate pinning or strict CA validation is enforced on DoH channels to prevent interception or use of unauthorized resolvers.

dns_monitoring_bypass_risk.title: Network DNS Monitoring Bypassed by DoH
dns_monitoring_bypass_risk.description: Whether existing network-level DNS monitoring controls (e.g., DNS firewall, RPZ, IDS DNS inspection) are effectively bypassed because DoH traffic flows outside monitored plaintext DNS paths.

qname_minimisation_enabled.title: QNAME Minimisation Enabled
qname_minimisation_enabled.description: Whether the recursive resolver is configured to send only the minimum necessary query name labels to each authoritative server hop per RFC 7816, rather than the full FQDN.

internal_domains_resolved.title: Internal Domains Resolved via External Recursion
internal_domains_resolved.description: Whether the resolver forwards or recurses queries for internal hostnames through external resolver hops such that internal FQDNs reach public resolvers or intermediate recursive infrastructure outside the organisation's control.

dns_source_rate_limiting_enabled.title: DNS Source-Based Rate Limiting Enabled
dns_source_rate_limiting_enabled.description: Indicates whether the DNS resolver or firewall enforces per-source IP query rate limits (e.g., RRL or equivalent ACL-based throttling) to prevent volumetric query floods.

dns_resolver_max_queries_per_second.title: DNS Resolver Max Queries Per Second (Per Source)
dns_resolver_max_queries_per_second.description: The configured maximum number of DNS queries per second allowed from a single source IP. A value of 0 indicates no limit is enforced.

rpki_validation_enabled.title: RPKI Validation Enabled
rpki_validation_enabled.description: Whether Resource Public Key Infrastructure (RPKI) Route Origin Validation is enforced on BGP peers that carry DNS traffic routes, preventing unauthorized route announcements from being accepted.

bgp_route_filtering_policy.title: BGP Route Filtering Policy
bgp_route_filtering_policy.description: The level of route filtering applied to BGP announcements for paths carrying DNS resolver traffic, indicating whether prefix lists or IRR-based filters are in place.

dns_traffic_uses_encrypted_transport.title: DNS Traffic Uses Encrypted Transport
dns_traffic_uses_encrypted_transport.description: Whether DNS client-to-resolver communications are protected by an encrypted and authenticated transport (DoT, DoH, or DoQ), which mitigates the impact of BGP hijacking by preventing an attacker-controlled resolver from silently intercepting plaintext queries.
